key_insight: The paper reframes mini-batch gradient estimation as a survey-sampling problem and uses auxiliary gradient-prediction models to reduce variance without changing the optimizer’s core update rule.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a drop-in way to improve training stability and efficiency in deep learning systems, especially when working with momentum-based optimizers.
method: Treat the dataset as a finite population and mini-batch gradients as sample-based estimates.
Use model-assisted sampling with auxiliary gradient predictors to build lower-variance gradient estimators.
Retain existing optimizers such as SGD or AdamW, with uniform sampling as the no-auxiliary baseline.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic data and six benchmark datasets report gains in 71–86% of runs, with especially strong results for medium-sized input spaces and improved generalization with AdamW in about half the training epochs.
watch_item: The approach adds an auxiliary prediction model, so its benefit may depend on the quality of the predictor and could introduce overhead if the model is poorly matched to the dataset.
paper_title: Stochastic Gradient Optimization with Model-Assisted Sampling
